newsitem.title: USA: NCAA-CHATTANOOGA, PROVIDENCE SCORE UPSETS, COPPIN STATE DOESN'T.
newsitem.headline: NCAA-CHATTANOOGA, PROVIDENCE SCORE UPSETS, COPPIN STATE DOESN'T.

text.p: The Chattanooga Choo-Choo kept on chugging and Providence dunked Duke but Cinderella Coppin State fell just short of the greatest upset in NCAA men's basketball history Sunday.
In other, milder second-round reversals of the seedings, Stanford ended the college career of Maryland's Tim Duncan and Louisville toppled New Mexico to advance to the Sweet 16.

At the Southeast Regionals at Charlotte, Willie Young scored 15 points as 14th-seeded Chattanooga stormed past sixth-seeded Illinois 75-63, inspired indirectly by 10th-seeded Providence's 98-87 victory over second seed Duke.

"We heard Illinois in the locker room next to us before the game carrying on after they heard Providence had won, screaming things like they're in the Final Four," said Chattanooga forward Johnny Taylor. "That really got under our skin and we really wanted to go out there and send a message."

The Moccasins (24-10), who are in the Sweet 16 for the first time in school history, became just the second 14th seed to advance out of the second round. Cleveland State did it in 1986 and immediately lost to Navy in the regional semifinals.
Chattanooga closed the game with a 16-4 run and held the Fighting Illini scoreless for six and a half minutes late in the second half.
Chattanooga will play Providence at Birmingham, Alabama, on Friday.
Providence's victory over Duke was built on Derrick Brown's career-high 33 points.
"I can't even think of the adjectives which you will think of to describe Brown's play," said Duke coach Mike Krzyzewski. "He was a great player today."

Austin Croshere hit a 12-foot bank shot with 5:09 to play to snap a tie and finished with 21 points for the Friars, in the Sweet 16 for the first time since reaching the Final Four in 1987. Providence broke the game open with a late 11-1 run.
The Southeast has lost two of its top four seeds. Top-ranked Kansas and fourth-seeded Arizona are in the other regional semifinal.
In the East Region at Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Reggie Freeman scored 22 points and made a key block as 10th-seeded Texas hung on for an 82-81 win over 15th-seeded Coppin State.
Kris Clack added 17 points for the Longhorns, who play Louisville Friday in Syracuse, New York.

Antoine Brockington scored 27 points and Terquin Mott added 17 for Coppin State (22-9), which was trying to become the first 15th seed in the Sweet 16. The Eagles were just the third 15th seed ever to advance to the second round.

"We knew we were facing a great team with a lot of talent, plus if this place holds 17,000, we were going to have like 16,800 cheering for the upset darlings of the tournament," said Longhorns coach Tom Penders. "So we knew that, and we're very fortunate to come out a winner."

"I'm real proud of the way they played, the character they exhibited out there, and how they wouldn't quit," said Coppin State coach Ron "Fang" Mitchell. "I'm real disappointed right now for them because they put in such a tremendous effort."

Freeman swatted the ball out of Danny Singletary's hands as he went up for a potential game-winner with 4.2 seconds to play. "It was Bronx playground defence," said Freeman. "He went by me and he thought he had an open lane, but I came behind him and blocked the shot."
Coppin State then set up a final play, but DeJuan Vazquez stole the inbounds pass and time expired.
In the other game, Alex Sanders had a key putback in the final minute as sixth-seeded Louisville edged third seed New Mexico 64-63.
DeJuan Wheat scored 22 points to lead Louisville, in the Sweet 16 for the second consecutive season as a sixth seed.
Charles Smith scored 16 points for New Mexico. The Lobos had a chance to win the game in the closing seconds, but David Gibson's running six-footer bounced high off the glass.

Only top-seeded North Carolina remains out of the top four seeds in the East Region. Second seed South Carolina lost in the first round while third-seeded New Mexico and fourth-seeded Villanova lost in round two.

In the West Region at Tucson, Arizona, Peter Sauer hit consecutive jumpers and Arthur Lee added a key tip-in in the final two minutes as sixth-seeded Stanford edged third-seeded Wake Forest 72-66, using tough physical play to control Duncan.
Stanford, which has won six straight games, reached the regional semifinals for the first time since 1942, the year of its only NCAA Tournament.

Duncan, the consensus choice for player of the year honours and widely praised for staying in school for his senior year, finished with 18 points and 20 rebounds but had just a bucket and two free throws in the second half.
The Cardinal will face second-seeded Utah, which beat seventh seed North Carolina Charlotte 77-58 as Keith Van Horn scored 27 points and grabbed eight rebounds.
In the Midwest Region at Kansas City, Missouri, Terrell McIntyre scored 16 points and fourth-seeded Clemson held fifth-seeded Tulsa's star Shea Seals to just five points in a 65-59 win.
Clemson will face top-seeded Minnesota, which beat ninth seed Temple 76-57.
